current_experiment_boundary.metadata_preflight_binding: existing fixed historical R24 preflight only

accepted_version_change_gate.if_r28_or_other_version_adopted_first: Create a NEW fixed plan binding its accepted source commit/tree, complete source map, actual baseline ELF, original qualification/harness, required test inventory and all hashes. Do not overwrite the existing R24 preparation or reuse the R24 220-count/ELF/test totals as latest-baseline evidence.

minimal_driver_change_set.details: Preserve the original qualify.py and all original 19 harness files in the source copy. Retain copyright/SPDX in the new external driver; bind original driver SHA, exact diff and actual new driver SHA in additional report fields. The unchanged 19-file snapshots do not establish that the executed driver is byte-identical to the old harness.

minimal_driver_change_set.change: Clean fixed environment and explicit flags after cleanup
minimal_driver_change_set.details: Replace inherited environment copying with a minimal allowlist; retain original test/worker settings. After cleanup insert only the frozen extra Rust CPU args through CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS. No inherited CARGO_PROFILE_*, CARGO_TARGET_*, CARGO_BUILD_*, RUST* or CARGO_ENCODED_* value is copied; explicitly required Cargo/Rustup toolchain selectors are reconstructed from reviewed pins.

Add reviewed host --target and -vv only to clippy/test-build/release. Retain test JSON; add release JSON. Keep all-target/all-feature/locked/offline scopes and all eight stages. Do not add global opt-level/LTO/panic flags to test builds.

Original --target driver option means target DIRECTORY. Add a separately named --target-triple or plan field; never overload it. Release outputs become <target-directory>/<triple>/release/{hepta-runtime,hepta-runtime-jobctl,examples/native_process_driver}. Derive and cross-check with actual Cargo artifact events; no fallback to an older release directory.

explicit_values_after_cleanup.HOME: verified original build-account home, not repurposed as candidate workspace
explicit_values_after_cleanup.CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: frozen value, original R24 actual was 2
explicit_values_after_cleanup.CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS: join fixed [-C, target-cpu=<unselected until metadata>] with ASCII 0x1f
explicit_values_after_cleanup.RUSTUP_HOME: verified installed toolchain home only if using pinned rustup shim
explicit_values_after_cleanup.RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL: 0 if using the reviewed rustup path

ambient_values_not_inherited: all CARGO_* except explicit reconstructed entries
all RUST* except explicit reconstructed entries
environment_design.recording: Record the constructed allowlist and command argv; never dump os.environ or credentials. Removed-variable families can be counted/named without values. Cargo may intentionally generate internal build-script/compiler variables; record normal outputs rather than rejecting expected Cargo/Clippy-generated internals.
environment_design.config_guard: A fresh CARGO_HOME alone does not exclude ancestor/project Cargo config. Bind the applicable config inputs and safe relevant settings; require no unreviewed profile, target, rustflags, linker, wrapper or forced [env] override. Do not modify system/user config to satisfy the experiment; stop preparation or choose already-authorized clean isolation when this cannot be established.
environment_design.release_profile: Keep accepted Cargo.toml unchanged: opt-level=3, lto=true/fat, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip=true, overflow-checks=false; verify observed final release invocation. Leave original dev/test profile and unwind fixtures intact.

initial_config_policy.paths: From the actual Cargo cwd (the full copied source root), inspect only metadata for both .cargo/config and .cargo/config.toml at that directory and every ancestor through filesystem root, plus both forms in selected private CARGO_HOME.
initial_config_policy.accepted_absence: Only definite not-found counts as absence. An existing unbound regular file, symlink, permission failure or other indeterminate path stops preparation. No file body or secret config value is printed or silently edited/renamed.
initial_config_policy.present_configuration: Permit only an explicitly pre-reviewed safe configuration with its own identity and permitted-key policy in a NEW fixed plan; the first minimal template has no such exception.
initial_config_policy.known_gap: Current metadata preflight hashes source-local Cargo configs only; that does not prove ancestor/user config absence.
initial_config_policy.no_cwd_workaround: Do not silently change cwd and add --manifest-path; that would change the original stage argv/cwd and fmt handling and needs a separately reviewed recipe.

stages.change: explicit target and verbose evidence only
explicit target and verbose evidence; preserve cargo-no-run.jsonl and original retention/parser
explicit target plus command/artifact evidence; no scope reduction

isolation_and_binding: Create a fresh owned run root only after native handoff, metadata closure and new fixed-plan approval path; separate source, target, Cargo cache, driver, qualification output and evidence directories. No prior artifact overwrites or hardlinks to mutable original inputs.

Copy the exact accepted source and original tools; verify full source map and separate tool manifest before/after. Compiler-only means no production Rust/Cargo/lock/source changes; any formatting byte change stops that claim for review.

Populate only verified offline dependency cache data needed by Cargo.lock in the private Cargo home; no target/fingerprint reuse from old builds, no credential files copied or logged, no downloads/tool install implied.

Use the original selected test inventory and ignored list for the source accepted at build time; execute all required tests and keep original no-retry behavior. R24 historical counts are not an R28 requirement.

Bind actual accepted baseline ELF bytes and SHA before comparison, plus each new release/test executable, source map, tools, configs and logs. Preserve every failed attempt under its original identity.

All release bins/examples are still built. A CPU-specific controller artifact does not confer portability on a rebuilt jobctl/driver; freeze deployment scope and existing remote helper identities separately before adoption.

Private cache population means verified offline dependency source/index/archive data only. It does not prove CPU compatibility and does not justify generic compiled artifact reuse; --target/CPU changes may require widespread rebuilding in the fresh target.

evidence_recipe.first_choice: No compiler wrapper. Keep raw Cargo -vv stdout/stderr, test and release Cargo JSON, source/config/driver hashes and selected actual product fingerprint files.
mandatory_checks: Actual required root release products come from this fresh run; match artifact path/name/profile/features and hash full bytes.
Observed final release compiler invocation includes the selected target/CPU plus retained release profile; do not require host proc macros or test fixtures to carry release-only flags.
Cargo JSON profile/artifact metadata is not a lossless complete rustc argv log. Cross-link it to verbose command evidence and actual output bytes.
Fingerprint rustflags[] is corroborating metadata if present, not a substitute for source/profile/command identity; preserve raw bytes and avoid assuming an invariant internal schema.
Missing or ambiguous effective flags fail evidence closure; do not fill gaps from the plan.
Very verbose logs include build-script output; preserve originals and hashes, apply existing publication scan policy, and never erase failed outcomes because a log cannot be published.
evidence_recipe.report_layout: Keep original eight-stage report keys and stage names for existing auditors, add a versioned compiler_recipe/driver block or companion build-evidence JSON. Original harness_before/after is labeled preserved source-harness identity; actual external driver/diff is recorded separately. New qualified/binary fields are written only after real execution.
minimal_extra_files: external-driver source plus exact diff and SHA
cargo-release.jsonl (or original release stdout with JSON) and raw stage logs

conditions: Explicitly inject a pinned RUSTC_WRAPPER after the new driver environment construction for the intended compile stage; an outer wrapper variable is removed by the original qualifier.
Keep RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER unset; published Cargo semantics and retained R19 history show workspace-wrapper metadata/identity effects.

A recorder may write a bounded per-invocation argv/cwd/stage identity record, never the ambient environment, then exec the exact compiler with unchanged arguments; logging failure must fail the build rather than silently omit evidence.
If attached across Clippy as well, the recorder must account for the intended Clippy driver/tool chain; a simplistic actual-rustc-only allowlist can reject legitimate Clippy commands.
Freeze recorder identity/path and treatment in any matched control. Do not assume a wrapped rebuild is byte/metadata-neutral relative to historical R24.
Use a new fixed recipe if wrapper instrumentation becomes necessary; do not mutate an already frozen qualifier or reinterpret a previous build.

comparison_scope.deployment_comparison: Qualified candidate versus actual accepted baseline under unchanged gates.
comparison_scope.cpu_flag_causality: Source-byte equality does not isolate CPU flags: historical R24 complete effective flags are not established, and a clean rebuild/explicit target/output mode may differ. Attribute only product-level results unless metadata proves the baseline recipe equivalence or a separately frozen matched control is actually built. No matched-control build is selected here.

plan_identity.scope: prepared observation/lifecycle gates; unchanged by this note

lifecycle_gates.controller_own_cpu_limit: A total plus original one tick per selected B phase per round; no new tolerance

frozen_gates_reference.rebinding_if_baseline_changes: New plan/version, not edits to historical R24 metadata or its reported results.

implementation_handoff: Only a local driver/template may be prepared next, with target CPU/triple, current accepted version and future qualification pins unresolved. It must refuse execution until the new frozen binding and native handoff exist. No native candidate has been scheduled by this design.
